correctness.rationale: Maximal matchings in \(K_{3,n}\) must saturate the three-vertex side; hence independent-dominating sets of \(K_3\square K_n\) have exactly three cells. This makes every coalition block size at most two. Fewer than three two-cell blocks leaves a singleton in every row without one of three necessary complementary row types. With exactly three blocks and \(n\ge4\), all rows have singleton cells, giving one pair per missing row. The three forced two-element column-set equations have exactly two solution types with counts \(n(n-1)\) and \(n(n-1)(n-2)\). At \(n=3\), sorted missing-row compositions \((1,1,1)\), \((0,1,2)\), \((0,0,3)\) yield 12, 36, 6 configurations by direct combinatorics. Complete enumeration of all 21147 set partitions at \(n=3\) and exhaustive near-maximal searches for \(n=4,\ldots,8\) independently corroborate the proof. No finite test is used as proof for unbounded \(n\).

value.rationale: The family \(K_3\square K_n\), the first nontrivial narrow rook products for coalition partitions, has a natural matching description and an exact leading polynomial coefficient. The structural classification distinguishes two-column and three-column optimal templates, and the square case has extra optimizer types. The exact value improves the existing \(2n\) idomatic lower and \(3n-1\) general upper bounds, a motivated growing quantitative gap. The public 2026 counting preprint expressly identifies Cartesian products as an open direction; this is a complete infinite-family classification, not a routine numeric recomputation.
